course.narrative: A 38-year-old right-handed female laborer presented for evaluation of allowed right medial epicondylitis and right carpal tunnel syndrome, and contested right cubital tunnel syndrome, following an injury over a period of time from performing normal job processes. She reported constant pain in the olecranon and distal triceps, tingling in the right long, ring, and small fingers, and night pain, exacerbated by gripping or opening jars. Records and diagnostic studies including EMG were reviewed. Physical examination revealed tenderness over the medial epicondyle, olecranon, and ulnar nerve, with diminished sensation in the right ring and small fingers, and a positive elbow flexion test. She was currently taking Aleve.
